claims.text: SRO suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated RHEAs at intermediate temperatures below 1000 K.
Diffuse antiphase boundaries associated with SRO are strong phonon-scattering centers.
Above about 1500 K, thermal energy overcomes the ordering-energy barrier and effectively melts SRO in MoNbTaW.
High-temperature loss of SRO restores phonon mean free paths.
A chemically short-range-ordered state of MoNbTaW can be equilibrated at approximately 800 K.
Disruption of local chemical order by screw-dislocation glide in MoNbTaW creates DAPB segments.
The SRO-related DAPB energy adds an enthalpic cost to kink-pair nucleation and strengthens MoNbTaW against screw-dislocation motion.
Potential fluctuations at DAPBs strongly scatter phonons and thereby reduce lattice thermal conductivity.
Lattice distortion and defects such as grain boundaries and dislocations can depress electron or phonon propagation in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The entropy term in the activation free energy makes the mechanical strengthening effect of SRO in MoNbTaW diminish at high temperature.
The entropy term in the free energy barrier reduces the thermodynamic stability of the SRO state itself.
When temperature exceeds an alloy's order-disorder transition temperature, its SRO parameters approach zero.
Loss of SRO makes DAPBs less distinct, reduces their phonon-scattering cross-section, and increases lattice thermal conductivity.
At 300 K, an SRO MoNbTaW sample should have significantly lower lattice thermal conductivity than a chemically equivalent random solid solution.
The thermal-conductivity difference between SRO and RSS MoNbTaW should narrow or vanish near 2000 K.
At 2000 K, the screw-dislocation mobility responses of simulated SRO and RSS MoNbTaW essentially overlap.
Quenching MoNbTaW from 800 K will produce a stable SRO specimen, whereas quenching it from above 1500 K will produce an RSS specimen.
APT or diffuse X-ray scattering can be used to measure an SRO parameter during the proposed temperature study.
Laser-flash analysis or time-domain thermoreflectance directly yields the lattice component of thermal conductivity.
If the SRO specimen has higher conductivity than the RSS specimen at low temperature, that result would favor an ordering-dominated regime in which SRO reduces mass-disorder scattering.

contradictions.description: The main mechanism interprets the high-temperature attenuation as melting or thermodynamic loss of SRO, whereas the cited MoNbTaW dislocation studies held the SRO state fixed and attributed attenuation to the entropy dependence of the kink-pair activation barrier. These are distinct mechanisms.

The boundary states that the hypothesis holds below the ODTT, while the predicted outcome extends the claimed convergence mechanism to approximately 2000 K without establishing the MoNbTaW ODTT or whether SRO remains present at that temperature.
